questions.question: Which of the following is the most common cause of microcytic hypochromic anemia worldwide?
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency anemia is the single most common cause of microcytic hypochromic anemia worldwide.

questions.question: Reed-Sternberg cells (owl-eyed appearance) are the characteristic diagnostic hallmark of:
questions.explanation: Reed-Sternberg cells are neoplastic giant cells characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma.

questions.question: The Philadelphia chromosome involving t(9;22) translocation is characteristically associated with:
questions.explanation: t(9;22) generates the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene, defining Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML).

questions.question: A 25-year-old female presents with fatigue and jaundice. Blood smear reveals spherocytes and Coombs test is positive. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Positive Coombs test (direct antiglobulin) differentiates autoimmune hemolytic anemia from hereditary spherocytosis.

questions.question: Bence-Jones proteins in the urine are characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Bence-Jones proteins represent free immunoglobulin light chains filtered into the urine in Multiple Myeloma.

pharmacology.title: 💊 Pharmacology (علم الأدوية)
pharmacology.description: مضادات التخثر ومثبطات الصفائح وأدوية فقر الدم

questions.question: What is the primary mechanism of action of Unfractionated Heparin?
questions.explanation: Heparin binds Antithrombin III and accelerates its inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa.

questions.question: Which of the following is the specific antidote for Warfarin-induced excessive anticoagulation?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K1 restores synthesis of functional clotting factors II, VII, IX, and X. Protamine is for Heparin.

questions.question: Which antiplatelet drug works by irreversible inhibition of Cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1)?
questions.explanation: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet COX-1, preventing Thromboxane A2 formation.

questions.question: What is the antidote used to reverse the anticoagulant effect of Heparin?
questions.explanation: Protamine sulfate is a strongly basic peptide that chemically neutralizes acidic heparin.

questions.question: Which drug is an iron chelating agent used in the treatment of chronic iron overload (hemochromatosis)?
questions.explanation: Deferoxamine binds free iron and is excreted in urine, treating iron toxicity and overload.

microbiology.title: 🧫 Microbiology (علم الأحياء الدقيقة)
microbiology.description: عدوى الدم والجهاز اللمفاوي والبكتيريا والطفيليات المسببة

questions.question: Which Plasmodium species is responsible for the most severe, fatal, and cerebral forms of Malaria?
questions.explanation: Plasmodium falciparum parasitizes RBCs of all ages, causing severe cytoadherence and cerebral malaria.

questions.question: Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV), the cause of Infectious Mononucleosis, primarily infects which cell type?
questions.explanation: EBV attaches to the complement receptor CD21 (CR2) on B lymphocytes.

questions.question: Which microorganism is the most frequent causative agent of acute infective endocarditis in intravenous drug users?
questions.explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is the most common cause of acute right-sided (tricuspid) endocarditis in IV drug abusers.

questions.question: The presence of atypical reactive lymphocytes (Downey cells) in peripheral blood is most commonly seen in:
questions.explanation: Atypical lymphocytes seen in infectious mononucleosis are reactive CD8+ cytotoxic T cells combating EBV-infected B cells.

questions.question: Which intracellular protozoan parasite is transmitted via feline (cat) feces and can cause congenital blood/CNS infection?
questions.explanation: Toxoplasma gondii is transmitted from cats or undercooked meat and infects the reticuloendothelial system.
